title: Consciousness may be palpated uncertainty about one's own memories

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Consciousness may be palpated uncertainty about one's own memories

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Extending Solms's idea that consciousness is palpated uncertainty about the outside world, Levin hypothesizes that consciousness is palpated uncertainty about one's own memories and internal states.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 7. A Continuum: From Thoughts to Thinkers

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I propose to expand this idea, with the hypothesis that consciousness is palpated uncertainty about your own memories and internal states.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “7. A Continuum: From Thoughts to Thinkers”. Scope: Conscious agents

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-16: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.10

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: One can correlate confidence, interoception and conscious report, but those observations do not uniquely test this proposed identity. The wording supplies no refuting outcome distinct from rivals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No third-person measurement is specified that distinguishes consciousness as felt uncertainty about internal memories from competing accounts that predict the same uncertainty reports and neural activity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim concerns subjective identity rather than a distinct observable relation.

Palpated uncertainty is not operationally defined.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.05
data adequacy: 0.05
data existence: 0.15
operationalizability: 0.1
analysis feasibility: 0.15

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statement is a hypothesis about what consciousness is. Neural and behavioral correlates of uncertainty can be recorded, and they remain compatible with several rival theories. No existing dataset contains an observation that would confirm or refute this identification.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Uncertainty about memory could be proxied by metacognitive or physiological measures, but those measures would not distinguish this hypothesis from other theories that tie consciousness to uncertainty, prediction error, or internal monitoring.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Palpated uncertainty about memories is not separable from ordinary metacognition or recall failure.

Consciousness has no agreed measurement that would uniquely confirm this extension of Solms.
